tips.title: Use Default Value
tips.explanation: Returns the value of var if set and not null, otherwise returns default. The variable itself is not modified.
tips.why: Prevents errors from unset variables and provides sensible defaults without if/else blocks. Cleaner than: if [ -z "$1" ]; then name="guest"; fi

tips.title: Prefer [[ ]] Over [ ]
tips.explanation: Double brackets provide safer testing with no word splitting, no glob expansion, and support for && || operators and regex matching with =~.
tips.why: Prevents quote-related bugs that plague single brackets. Pattern matching works naturally without quotes. Much safer for variable testing.

tips.title: Exit on Error
tips.explanation: Exit immediately if any command fails (returns non-zero). Add at the start of scripts to prevent cascading failures from unnoticed errors.
tips.example:
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd /nonexistent  # Script stops here
echo "Never reached"
tips.why: Catches errors early before they compound. Without this, failed commands silently continue and cause confusing downstream issues. Essential for production scripts.
